newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil heading for social security deficit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil heading for social security deficit in 1997.

text.p: Brazil's social security system is heading for a deficit of roughly one billion reais ($934 million) in 1997, contrary to earlier expectations of equilibrium, a senior Finance Ministry official said.
"Certainly, the National Treasury will have to provide money for the social security system if this forecast proves correct," said Pedro Parente, the ministry's executive secretary.

Contributions had proved lower than expectations, partly because of the introduction of a new, single corporate tax for small companies and also because mayors who took office in January had temporarily halted municipal payments.
In 1996, the INSS social security system paid $500 million more in benefits than it received in contributions.

Parente, speaking to reporters at a seminar on public finance, said the government maintained its target of finishing 1997 with a 1.5 percent surplus in the primary fiscal account, which does not include debt costs.

A predicition by Planning Minister Antonio Kandir that Brazil might this year cut its operational deficit, which includes debt costs, to three percent was compatible with a 1.5 percent surplus in the primary account, the official said.

States and municipalities had improved their fiscal performance, reducing an operational deficit equivalent to 0.8 percent of gross domestic product in the first half of 1996 to about 0.3 percent in the January-June period this year, he said.
